campaign.name: CSS children via code-calculus v0.2 sector swap, support search, and bounded sector search

direction.hypothesis: Using code-calculus v0.2's E-LOCAL-HADAMARD sector swap at T=Q (which exchanges the stronger sector into the target at unchanged full distance) together with bounded support search and Pareto ranking, CSS children of board entries with n <= 120 reach frontier points that the v0.1 single-move campaigns missed because they could not exploit a stronger opposite sector.

bar.note: best kd^2/n among unrestricted weight-6 entries with n <= 100

direction.feasibility: The v0.2 consumer exposes sector_swap, support_search, bounded_sector_search, and Pareto ranking; parents are the board's CSS entries with n <= 120, and the gate validates children unchanged.

novelty.claim: CSS children reached by a sector swap followed by peel/puncture/deletion, with the stronger sector exploited for a target-sector distance gain
novelty.against: the v0.1 campaigns of fieldnotes/2026-11-02-code-calculus-v0p1-campaigns.md, which used only single moves and no sector swap

direction.expected_value: A child whose target-sector distance improves after a sector swap would be the first evidence that E-LOCAL-HADAMARD at T=Q pays on this board; the full distance is unchanged, so the gain is in which sector carries the bound.

abandon_criterion.note: drop a parent lineage once two fresh-seed rungs agree below the parent's distance

direction.what_a_negative_would_teach: That exploiting the stronger sector via a swap does not create board-advancing children at these sizes, so the v0.1 result (zero E-LOCAL-HADAMARD survivors) stands even with the v0.2 search machinery.

campaign.notes: Uses code-calculus-dev at its latest commit for sector_swap, support_search, bounded_sector_search, run_campaign, and Pareto ranking. See research/audits for the reachability record.
